diagnostic_item.correct_answer: Yes — they are equivalent, the same amount

distractors.value: No, 2/4 is bigger because the numbers are bigger
No, they look different so they can't be equal

diagnostic_item.stem: Two identical circles are shaded the same amount, but one is cut into 2 parts (1 shaded) and the other into 4 parts (2 shaded). Are 1/2 and 2/4 the same amount?

intervention.script: Let's stack a bar split in halves on top of one split in fourths — see how the shaded amount lines up exactly.

learner_evidence.explanation: yes they're the same because you just cut the second one into smaller pieces but it's still the same amount shaded

caveats: transfer confirmed on a number line only; set-model transfer not yet attempted

misconception.citation: Literature on componential vs. proportional reasoning in fraction equivalence.
misconception.cognitive_origin: Children treat numerator and denominator as independent whole-number counts, so scaling both by the same factor looks like making a different, bigger fraction rather than preserving the same part-whole ratio — a failure to see multiplicative equivalence.
misconception.title: Scaling numerator and denominator together changes a fraction's value

sprout_scripts.utterance: 1/2 and 2/4 can't be the same — 2/4 has bigger numbers, so it must be more!
Wait, how can two different-looking fractions be the exact same amount?
If the numbers are different, doesn't that mean the fractions are different too?
